entries.name: ABAP
entries.definition: SAP's proprietary programming language for writing business applications that run on SAP systems.

entries.name: ActionScript
entries.definition: An object-oriented programming language based on ECMAScript, used mainly for Adobe Flash and AIR applications.

entries.name: Ada
entries.definition: A statically typed, structured programming language designed for reliable, long-lived embedded and safety-critical software.

entries.name: Ada 95
entries.definition: The 1995 revision of the Ada programming language (ISO/IEC 8652:1995), which added object-oriented features to Ada 83.

entries.name: Afrikaans
entries.definition: A West Germanic language that developed from Dutch, spoken mainly in South Africa and Namibia.

entries.name: Ainu
entries.definition: A critically endangered language of the Ainu people of northern Japan.

entries.name: Akan
entries.definition: A language spoken mainly in Ghana, with varieties such as Twi and Fante.

entries.name: Albanian
entries.definition: An Indo-European language forming its own branch, spoken mainly in Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia.

entries.name: Algebraic Logic Functional
entries.definition: A programming language that combines functional and logic programming.

entries.name: ALGOL
entries.definition: A family of imperative programming languages first designed in 1958, whose ALGOL 60 and ALGOL 68 versions influenced many later languages.

entries.name: American Sign Language
entries.definition: A sign language used mainly by Deaf communities in the United States and English-speaking Canada.

entries.name: Amharic
entries.definition: A Semitic language spoken mainly in Ethiopia, where it is the working language of the federal government.

entries.name: AMPscript
entries.definition: Salesforce Marketing Cloud's scripting language for personalizing the content of emails, landing pages and other messages.

entries.name: Apex
entries.definition: A strongly typed, object-oriented programming language for writing business logic on the Salesforce platform.

entries.name: Arabic
entries.definition: A Semitic language spoken across the Middle East and North Africa, with a standard written form used in formal settings.

entries.name: ArchiMate
entries.definition: An open modelling language, maintained by The Open Group, for describing enterprise architecture across business, application and technology layers.

entries.name: Armenian
entries.definition: An Indo-European language forming its own branch, spoken mainly in Armenia and by Armenian communities abroad.

entries.name: ASP.NET Razor
entries.definition: A markup syntax from Microsoft for embedding C# or Visual Basic code in HTML to generate web pages on the server.

entries.name: Assamese
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken mainly in the Indian state of Assam.

entries.name: Assembly language
entries.definition: A family of low-level programming languages in which each statement corresponds closely to a machine instruction of a particular processor.

entries.name: AWK
entries.definition: A scripting language for processing text line by line with pattern-action rules, named after its creators Aho, Weinberger and Kernighan.

entries.name: Aymara
entries.definition: An indigenous language of the Andes spoken mainly in Bolivia, Peru and Chile.

entries.name: Azerbaijani
entries.definition: A Turkic language spoken mainly in Azerbaijan and northwestern Iran.

entries.name: Ballerina
entries.definition: An open-source programming language for writing cloud-native integration and network-service programs, created by WSO2.

entries.name: Base SAS
entries.definition: The core of the SAS system, providing the SAS programming language with its DATA step, procedures and macro facility for data management and analysis.

entries.name: Bash
entries.definition: The GNU Project's Unix shell and its scripting language, the default shell on many Linux systems.

entries.name: BASIC
entries.definition: A family of high-level programming languages first designed in 1964 at Dartmouth College to be easy for beginners.

entries.name: Bassa
entries.definition: A Kru language of Liberia spoken by the Bassa people, not to be confused with the Bantu language Basaa of Cameroon.

entries.name: Batak
entries.definition: A group of related Austronesian languages spoken by the Batak peoples of northern Sumatra, Indonesia.

entries.name: BeanShell
entries.definition: A lightweight scripting language for the Java platform that interprets Java syntax with extra scripting features.

entries.name: Bemba
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken mainly in northern Zambia and nearby parts of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

entries.name: Benga
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken along the coast of Equatorial Guinea and Gabon.

entries.name: Bengali
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken mainly in Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal.

entries.name: Berber
entries.definition: A family of related Afro-Asiatic languages spoken across North Africa, also known as the Amazigh languages.

entries.name: Bislama
entries.definition: An English-based creole language and one of the national languages of Vanuatu.

entries.name: BlitzMax
entries.definition: A BASIC-derived, object-oriented programming language aimed at game development, created by Blitz Research.

entries.name: Boo
entries.definition: An object-oriented, statically typed programming language for the .NET common language infrastructure, with a Python-inspired syntax.

entries.name: Bosnian
entries.definition: A South Slavic language, one of the official languages of Bosnia and Herzegovina, closely related to Croatian and Serbian.

entries.name: Burmese
entries.definition: A Sino-Tibetan language, the official language of Myanmar.

entries.name: C++
entries.definition: Writing programs in C++.
